Thank you all for these critical findings. Let me synthesize what I'm hearing and outline how I plan to proceed before finalizing my decision.

First, on the collateral gap: Harish, the eligible collateral only supports $14 million against a $20 million facility. That's a $6 million shortfall. Maya's sponsor equity injection of $3 million, if unconditional and documented, could partially bridge that gap — but it doesn't fully close it. I need to understand whether the $3 million equity injection is intended to serve as additional collateral support or whether it's purely a balance sheet enhancement.

Second, on cash dominion: Jonas has identified a mandatory legal trigger — the intercreditor agreement requires cash dominion whenever utilization exceeds 75% of committed availability. With only $14 million in eligible collateral against a $20 million facility, utilization could easily exceed that 75% threshold. The draft renewal package is currently silent on this, and that's an unacceptable gap. Cash dominion terms must be incorporated into the renewal amendment.

Third, on compliance: Tara has confirmed that a beneficial-ownership certification must be completed before the first post-renewal draw and refreshed annually. This needs to be added to the renewal checklist as a condition.

So here's where I land before I finalize: I cannot approve the package as currently drafted. The draft has no cash-funding condition, no cash-control terms, and no compliance terms — but we've now identified that all three are needed. Before I issue my decision, I need Maya to confirm: (1) the signed sponsor letter will be attached to the credit file today, and (2) whether the $3 million equity injection has any conditions attached. I also need Harish to upload the updated borrowing-base worksheet. Once I have those confirmations, I'll finalize the renewal terms incorporating the cash dominion trigger, the beneficial-ownership certification requirement, and appropriate sizing of the facility.
